strategyChanges.title: Shorten speculative branches and verify destination
strategyChanges.marker: ### Trial 5: Shorten speculative branches and verify the actual destination
strategyChanges.excerpt:
### Trial 5: Shorten speculative branches and verify the actual destination

The first five games show that lengthy unverified calculation has not prevented simple one-move losses. Before benchmark 6, revisit the last board mentally and name the actual black pawn captures: b6-a5/c5, c7-b6/d6, e5-d4/f4, f4-e3/g3, g7-f6/h6, h7-g6. In particular, c5 was attacked by b6 regardless of the king's protection of e5 or the knight's retreat. These are my own mechanical board observations, not an engine evaluation.

For benchmark 6, try a compact rule: after selecting a candidate, check the exact destination against every enemy pawn and knight before exploring longer continuations. Keep the full current board in view and do not substitute an imagined later board. This is a revised approach to test, not proof of learning. No additional practice for this trial; use the next fixed Black/1800 game as a new-position test, then the six-game review. Main target: no major piece placed directly onto an existing pawn capture square. Rook mobility and pawn forks remain unresolved.

strategyChanges.title: Immediate checks on resulting board
strategyChanges.marker: ### Trial 6: Verify the opponent's immediate checks on the resulting board
strategyChanges.excerpt:
### Trial 6: Verify the opponent's immediate checks on the resulting board

Next evaluation point: twelve scored benchmarks, with brief self-review after each intervening game and a method change sooner if the same error recurs. First undertake a short opponent-practice drill from game 6 after ply 63, explicit Black color, skill 3, at most four own moves. This is remembered, not new transfer evidence. My own candidate is Ke7, chosen mentally to avoid the immediate Qh8 mating net; it may concede the trapped bishop to fxe5, so this trial is about surviving a forcing attack, not preserving all material or finding a best move.

Then return to the fixed rotation. Before submitting a non-forcing move near an exposed king, reconstruct the resulting board and check the opponent's available immediate checks, including newly opened rook lines and controlled king destinations. The original destination check alone missed a move that was legal but removed the only escape square. Observable benchmark target: no repeated Qh8-style mate caused by uncovering a rook line, and fewer immediate major-piece losses. These targets are measured by accepted moves and outcomes, not by the length of my checklist.

Token accounting: an actual get_goal call after the six-game checkpoint reported 867114 cumulative tokens for the active goal. Its input/output accounting details are unavailable; this is the reported goal counter, not an invented thinking-token total or a fixed-budget claim. There is no token budget.

Practice 6 stopped after four own moves: Ke7, Kd7, Kc6, fxe5. Opponent replies were Bg6, Bf5+, fxe5, Kg1. The original immediate mating net was avoided, but my trapped dark-square bishop was lost for the f-pawn. Zero illegal submissions. This is a remembered local survival check at a mater

strategyChanges.title: Retain a blocker while changing king shelter
strategyChanges.marker: ### Trial 44: retain a blocker while changing king shelter
strategyChanges.excerpt:
### Trial 44: retain a blocker while changing king shelter

Choose next full evaluation at 54 scored games. First one remembered skill-10 Black practice from game 48 after ply 57, before 29...Nf8. Own candidate Kf6 instead, retaining Ne6's screen of Bd5–f7 and Qc8's guard of Rd8. Against an imagined Bxe6, Kxe6 is a candidate king recapture to inspect on the actual board, rather than automatically departing Qc8 and abandoning Rd8. Neither move is tested, proved safe/best or a forced defense. This is my own mental position study, not independent analysis. Cap drill at six own moves or natural finish. Targets: no blocked-flight mate, no abandoned major through a guardian departure, zero illegal submissions. Record actual replies even if they differ; a remembered local success is not transfer. Then fixed benchmarks 49–54 to measure recurrence and score; no indefinite repetitions.

### Trial 44 execution: practice 31

Correct game 48 ply 57, Black skill 10. Actual six own moves and replies: Kf6/Ne1, Kf7/Nf3, Bf6/Ng5+, Bxg5/hxg5, Ke8/Ra7, Nd4/Ra8. Explicitly stopped at the chosen cap, result *, twelve plies, zero illegal submissions; verified official practice PGN. No mate or major loss occurred during these replies. Bxg5/hxg5 balanced bishop for knight; the starting one-pawn deficit remained. Retaining Ne6 screened Bd5's f7 attack during Kf7, although it again pinned that knight temporarily. Ke8 released the pin and guarded Rd8; Nd4 then used c5's pawn support. Final Ra8 attacked Qc8, so this is not a quiet or fully defended final position. No seventh move selected or played. No extra repetitions.

Local preservation targets were met over six own moves against different skill-10 replies. The opponent never repeated benchmark Rxe7+/Kh6/Qd2/g5/hxg5+/Kg6/Be4+/Qf5/Nh4#. No repai
